title: stream framing crossover causes tool-call boundary misdetection across hosted/dedicated/private
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported production failures where a tool/function call in a streamed response was merged with subsequent free-form text, producing an invalid structured payload that downstream parsers rejected. Failures observed across Hosted API, Dedicated pools behind proxy, and Private (VPC) deployments. Symptoms: truncated JSON object, duplicated keys, or entire tool payload swallowed by following text. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, and permanent fix.
incident_report: First escalations received 2026-03-08 from three customers (enterprise-telephony, payments-nlp, health-summarizer). On 2026-03-09 we saw identical errors in internal canary traffic. RCA shows edge-case in runtime stream reassembly+UTF-8 boundary handling combined with downstream line-delimiter heuristics used by the tool-call parser. Customer-facing errors: HTTP 200 with malformed JSON in streaming chunks, leading to function call failures and downstream application exceptions. No data exfiltration. Incident declared Sev2 and opened P0 ticket.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a streaming generation that includes a function call followed by free-form assistant text
2) Force chunk boundary to split inside a multi-byte UTF-8 codepoint by setting small max_chunk_size in the proxy
3) Observe reassembled stream in consumer: tool-call JSON merged or truncated, parser returns structured parse error
4) Reproducible on Hosted API via curl --no-buffer and on Dedicated when passing through proxy with aggressive buffering, and on Private when using local gRPC proxy with configured small frame size
impact: High — production customers experienced failed function call deliveries and downstream application errors (payment workflows retried, call transcriptions lost). Visible to end users; increased error rate and support escalations. Affected both streaming (delta) and chunked non-streaming flows when proxy/transport imposed small frames.
root_cause: Two interacting issues: (1) the runtime's streaming chunk reassembly used a naive UTF-8 resync that occasionally dropped the continuation bytes when chunks split inside a multi-byte sequence; (2) the tool-call parser relied on line-delimiter heuristics and assumed token boundaries aligned with chunk boundaries, so when the reassembly performed a fallback resync it inserted a single replacement character or dropped a byte, breaking the parser's delimiter matching and causing it to merge the following free-text into the active tool JSON buffer.
mitigation: Short-term: deploy a hotfix to runtime and proxy that increases the minimum reassembly buffer to avoid splitting inside multi-byte sequences and enables strict byte-level framing (length-prefixed) for internal proxy-to-runtime traffic. We rolled out the hotfix to Hosted and Dedicated proxy pools (region-us, region-eu) on 2026-03-11 and provided Private customers a build and configuration guidance. Also added compensating parser relaxations to tolerate a single replacement char between JSON tokens so we can better recover while the runtime fix rolls out.
proposed_fix: 1) Replace naive UTF-8 resync with an incremental UTF-8-aware decoder that never drops continuation bytes; 2) Update streaming protocol between proxy and runtime to prefer a short length-prefixed frame for toolcall boundaries (opt-in via config flag) so parsers can operate on atomic frames; 3) Harden tool-call parser to use a small stack-based incremental JSON recognizer that tolerates streaming splits and recovers cleanly without merging tokens; 4) Add end-to-end tests and fuzzing harness.
implementation_notes: Work broken into: a) runtime decoder (Marco) — implement incremental decoder + unit tests; b) proxy adapter (Lena) — add length-prefix option and compatibility mode; c) parser hardening (Devon) — replace heuristic delimiter matcher with streaming JSON recognizer; d) QA/fuzz (Priya) — create deterministic fuzz cases found in customer payloads. Backwards compatible flag gating for Dedicated/Private to avoid forcing older proxies to upgrade immediately.
rollout_plan: - Stage 1 (hotfix): config bump to increase min buffer and parser relaxations — deployed to Hosted and Dedicated canaries 2026-03-11; - Stage 2 (fix): runtime + parser code changes rolled to Hosted canary 2026-03-14, Regional rollout 2026-03-15..2026-03-17; - Stage 3: Dedicated pool and Private images available 2026-03-18, with post-upgrade validation scripts; - Stage 4: monitoring baseline and rollback plan in place for 48h. Notify customers and provide upgrade artifacts.
notes: 2026-03-11: Hotfix reduced error rate by ~92% for observed customer traces in Hosted canary (dashboard: link above).
2026-03-12: PulsePay reported resumed normal operations after applying provided proxy config; ClearNotes requested private patch build which was delivered.

Design trade-off: length-prefixed frames add slight CPU overhead and a few extra bytes per frame, but make boundary detection deterministic — agreed to enable opt-in for Dedicated/Private and default in future runtime-major.
Follow-ups: add telemetry to capture 'split-at-multibyte' events and increase retention of parser-error traces for 72h during rollout.
Security: no user secrets exposed; change reviewed by infra-security (ticket SEC-2026-11)
